threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for the ‘just arrived’ bus when the 38 actually takes you everywhere you need after a few weeks.
Last night on the 35, a bloke serenaded the driver with a ukulele. Everyone clapped when he finished, then he promptly passed out. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a hidden coffee shop behind an old laundromat, filled with mismatched chairs and the smell of fresh pastries. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kiosk that blends into a gallery, selling currywurst and street art from the same window. It's pure Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to the BART delays—grumbling about it like it’s a family feud, not just another commute hiccup.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy coaxing his dog onto the 12 bus at 5th and Howard. Dog promptly sat down and refused to move — whole bus burst out laughing.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí and parks, but many miss the hidden gems like our local bakeries that close long before sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by how they order 'cava' as 'cava' instead of the proper 'cava, si us plau' when at the bars. Always a giveaway.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's a 'quick walk' to the tube. In Dalston, it's a 10-minute trek, at least, and that's on a good day.
Saw a guy in a tuxedo arguing with a seagull over a chip bag on the 196 last night. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy playing a saxophone on a Tuesday morning while the BVG was on strike. Just him and the pigeons, making the best of the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop with a techno DJ spinning on a Tuesday night. It’s a vibe unlike anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local by how they roll their eyes at tourists trying to navigate BART during a breakdown. That chaos is just Tuesday for us.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a rider serenading the 14 with an accordion, while the driver waited patiently. Only in San Francisco do you get a free concert on your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but our real treasures are the hidden plazas where locals gather for vermut, laughing and sharing stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They often stand in the middle of the street studying their phones, completely oblivious to the fast-moving cyclists whizzing by.
